display.purpose: Hero headline only; one word set in italic mocha-deep for emphasis instead of bold.

body.purpose: Running copy; a 1.125rem lead variant is used for intros and pull quotes.

note.purpose: Secondary copy between body and label — card descriptions, bios, footer tagline, button labels.

chip.purpose: Smallest step — category badges and image captions.

shadows.name: soft

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Hover state for cards/buttons; resting state for panel-level surfaces (booking form, hero media, sticky CTA).

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: Default easing for hover, reveal, and state transitions.

motion.name: ease-in-out-soft
motion.purpose: Used for symmetric open/close transitions (mobile menu, sticky CTA slide).

narrative.overview: VERVENA reads like an unhurried Lviv craftsperson's studio, not a salon chasing volume. The palette is warm and grounded — every neutral, including the near-black ones, carries a tint rather than sitting on true gray — and the two accent hues (mocha, and a much rarer olive/lavender) show up in small doses: a chip, a rule, a single CTA. Fraunces at a light weight gives headlines an editorial, slightly serif calm; Manrope carries the reading text. Nothing in the system shouts: no bold color fills, no hard shadows, no snap transitions. Depth and emphasis come from restraint — a hairline border, a soft warm-tinted shadow that only appears on interaction, a translate instead of a flash. The system explicitly rejects the visual vocabulary of a "conveyor-belt" salon: no countdown timers, no saturated banner blocks, no loud iconography, no inflated numbers. Motion is capped and physically eased; a whisper of film grain sits under everything as the only textural flourish, standing in for the tactility a photograph alone can't carry.
keyCharacteristics: Warm OKLCH neutrals (never true gray) paired with three rare, low-saturation accents (mocha, olive, lavender)
Fraunces (light weight, serif, editorial) for display type; Manrope for everything read at length
Flat-at-rest surfaces; shadows and lift are an interaction response, never a resting state
Physically-eased motion only (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) / cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)) — linear and default ease are banned
Soft, generous corners (1rem–1.5rem) everywhere except hairline dividers

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: No neutral in this system is true gray. Surfaces sit around hue 75 (warm), text sits around hue 240 (cool charcoal) — but even the darkest tones (ink, espresso) carry a visible tint, never #000-adjacent desaturation.

rules.name: The Rare Accent Rule
rules.body: Mocha, olive, and lavender never fill a large surface at full opacity. They appear as: a small rounded chip (/10–/25 opacity background), a 1px gradient rule, a single primary CTA, or a blurred, low-opacity ambient wash. The moment an accent covers more than a button or a chip, dilute it.

rules.name: The Legible Fill Rule
rules.body: mocha (62% lightness) is a hue, not a fill — it never sits behind porcelain text. Any solid button/chip/CTA fill carrying porcelain text uses mocha-deep at rest and mocha-deeper on hover, both ≥4.5:1 against porcelain.

rules.name: The Light Display Rule
rules.body: All headline-level type ships at font-weight 300 (Tailwind's font-light), even though the base stylesheet's h1–h4 rule declares 380 as an unstyled fallback. Emphasis inside a headline comes from italics and color (mocha-deep), never from added weight.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: A shadow is either a hover response or a signal that an element floats above the page by design (buttons, panels, the sticky bar). A passive content card at rest never carries one — only its mist border does the work.

dos: Do show every price plainly as "від {sum} ₴" next to its service — never hide pricing behind a "contact us" gate.
Do keep every tappable control (buttons, radio cards, chips) at a 48px+ minimum touch target.
Do reserve an image's aspect-ratio up front (the Figure component) so nothing shifts as photos load; CLS stays at zero.
Do pair every validation state with text + an icon, never color alone.
Do give every interactive element a visible focus-visible ring: 2px mocha, 3px offset.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion completely — all transitions and the scroll-reveal system collapse to instant with it on.
donts: Don't use linear or default ease-in-out easing anywhere; only the two physically-eased curves (ease-out-quart, ease-in-out-soft) are sanctioned.
Don't fill a large surface with a saturated accent color; mocha/olive/lavender stay in chips, rules, a single CTA, or low-opacity ambient washes.
Don't use aggressive urgency copy, countdown timers, or fake scarcity — the hero's one availability note is soft and informational, never a pressure tactic.
Don't let a scroll-reveal travel more than 20px or apply a hard shadow to a resting content card.

Don't invent or inflate numbers (review counts, client counts, ratings) — this system's honesty about being a fictional portfolio project depends on never dressing up the fake content as verified real evidence.
